summary.text: Mario Diaz-Balart is the Republican incumbent in Florida's 26th District and the dean of Florida's congressional delegation. A Fort Lauderdale native, he began in public service as an aide to the Miami mayor, served in the Florida Senate and House, and has been in the U.S. House since 2003. He is Vice Chair of the Appropriations Committee.

paragraphs.text: Díaz-Balart was born in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, on September 25, 1961, to Cuban parents. His father, Rafael Díaz-Balart, was a Cuban politician, and his brother Lincoln Díaz-Balart represented a Miami-area district in Congress from 1993 to 2011.
He studied political science at the University of South Florida and began his public service career in 1985 as an aide to the Mayor of Miami.

Díaz-Balart served in the Florida State Senate (District 37) from 1992 to 2000 and in the Florida House of Representatives (District 112) from 2000 to 2002; Wikipedia also says he was elected to the Florida House in 1988.
His official biography says he chaired several committees in the state legislature, including the Appropriations Committee.

Díaz-Balart was elected to the U.S. House in 2002 and has served since 2003 under successive district numbers as Florida's maps changed; he has represented the 26th District since 2023. His official biography describes him as fulfilling his 12th term and as the House Deputy Whip.
In the 2025-2026 Congress he serves on the House Appropriations Committee as Vice Chair and chairs the subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs.
He has been the dean of Florida's congressional delegation since April 2021, according to Wikipedia.
Díaz-Balart lives in Miami with his wife, Tia, and their son, according to his official biography.
